questions.title: Initialize and Print an Array
questions.description:
Create an array from user input and display it. Read n, then read n integers into an int array, and print all elements of the array on one line, separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n array elements separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Sum and Average of Array Elements
questions.description:
Read n integers into an array, then compute the total of all elements and their average. Print the total on the first line and the average rounded to exactly 2 decimal places on the second line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the sum of all elements.
Line 2: the average rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Smallest and Largest with Positions
questions.description:
Read n integers into an array and report where the smallest and largest values sit. Positions are 1-based and, when a value repeats, use the first position where it appears. Print two lines, one for the minimum and one for the maximum. Input Format: Line 1: n, the number of elements. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Output Format: Line 1: Min at position

Line 2: Max at position where p and q are the 1-based positions of the first occurrence of the minimum and maximum. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000
questions.sampleoutput1:
Min 5 at position 2
Max 30 at position 5
questions.sampleoutput2:
Min 3 at position 1
Max 3 at position 1
questions.output1:
Min -7 at position 2
Max 4 at position 5
questions.output2:
Min 99 at position 1
Max 99 at position 1
questions.output3:
Min -1 at position 2
Max 22 at position 4

questions.title: Enhanced For Loop Sum
questions.description:
Read n integers into an array, then compute the total of all elements using an ENHANCED for loop (for(int x : a)). The enhanced for loop visits every element of the array by value. Print the total.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the sum of all array elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Print Array in Reverse
questions.description:
Read n integers into an array and print them in reverse order (last element first) on one line, separated by single spaces. Do not modify the array; simply traverse it from the last index down to index 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n elements in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Copy Array and Print
questions.description:
Read n integers into a source array. Then create a second array of the same length and copy every element of the source into it with a loop (element by element, not by assigning references). Print both arrays on separate lines.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: Original: followed by the source elements separated by single spaces.
Line 2: Copy: followed by the copied elements separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Daily Temperature Log Statistics
questions.description:
A weather station logged the temperature of n consecutive days as integers. Analyze the log: print the hottest temperature, the coldest temperature, and the average temperature rounded to 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of days.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the temperatures.

Output Format:
Line 1: Hottest: <value>
Line 2: Coldest: <value>
Line 3: Average: <value rounded to exactly 2 decimal places>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= temperature <= 1000000

questions.title: Shopping Cart Item Totals
questions.description:
A billing counter scans the price of each item (an integer number of rupees) into an array. After storing all prices, the receipt is printed: one line per item showing its position and price, then a final line with the grand total.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of items.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the item prices.

Output Format:
One line per item: Item <i>: <price> (i starts from 1, in input order)
Final line: Total: <sum of all prices>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= price <= 100000
questions.output3:
Item 1: 0
Item 2: 15
Item 3: 0
Item 4: 25
Item 5: 10
Total: 50

questions.title: Attendance Eligibility Count
questions.description:
A college allows students to sit for the exam only if their attendance is 75 percent or more. The office stored the attendance percentage of each student in an array. Count how many students are eligible (attendance >= 75) and how many are not.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of students.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the attendance percentages.

Output Format:
Line 1: Eligible: <count of students with attendance >= 75>
Line 2: Not eligible: <count of students with attendance < 75>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= attendance <= 100

questions.title: Token Queue in Reverse Order
questions.description:
A clinic issues token numbers to patients in arrival order and stores them in an array. The display board above the door shows the latest token first, so the receptionist needs the token list printed in reverse order (last issued first). Print the tokens on one line, separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of tokens issued.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the token numbers in issue order.

Output Format:
One line with the token numbers in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= token <= 999999
